correctness.rationale: For every integer n≥r+1, r≥3, and 0<p<1, decomposing each triangle/centered-induced-star indicator pair by 0,1,2,3 shared vertices gives zero, zero, p^(r+2)q^C(r,2)[2-(r+1)p] for overlap two, and -(r+1)p^(r+3)q^C(r,2) for overlap three after summing over r+1 possible centers. Exact combinatorial counts produce the formula. The bracket is affine in p with unique zero when n≥r+2 and strictly negative at n=r+1; elementary differentiation yields both strict monotonicity results and direct ratio limits establish scaling. Standalone checker passed 3213 exact rational tests including exhaustive graphs n≤6, independently accumulated pair-indicator covariances n≤10, and threshold checks n≤79. These experiments corroborate; proof covers all n,r,p.

value.rationale: The triangle count is a canonical transitivity/closure statistic, whereas induced stars measure open hub-and-spoke structure. Their sign-changing co-fluctuation is a natural issue for joint graphlet significance: sparse edge densities reinforce both counts, dense regimes trade triangles against leaf independence. The theorem gives a complete all-star-size sign diagram, strict monotonicity in motif and graph sizes, and a nontrivial joint r/n scaling boundary. This is more than a single small graphlet count or a reparameterized variance formula; the uniform phase classification is the mathematically motivated contribution.
